title: Army Weekly Briefing
description: Army leadership, force design, modernization, contracts and the signal and network enterprise.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 26–Nov. 5. New: DVIDS posted Nov. 4 that Project Manager Terrestrial Sensors and Project Director Sensors Aerial Intelligence merged Nov. 1 into PM ATSR, and the Nov. 4 Department of War contracts release awarded Avum $61 million to refactor the Virtual Contracting Enterprise. The Oct. 29 Future Interceptor item was removed so the contracts subsection stayed at four. That release also listed an HHI repair at a San Antonio Reserve center and a Clark modification for a Fort Bliss clinic; those facilities actions were not added. No new NETCOM release was found. Federal News Network's homepage listed an Army National Guard childcare expansion and the CISA note already on the cyber page. EIN Presswire carried the sensor-office release; this item cites the DVIDS original. The Project Griffin pilot remains the WWT line.

items.headline: Army merges aerial and ground sensor offices into PM ATSR
items.summary: DVIDS posted Nov. 4, in a story by M. Scott Bortot, that on Nov. 1 Project Manager Terrestrial Sensors and Project Director Sensors Aerial Intelligence merged into Project Manager Aerial-Terrestrial Surveillance and Reconnaissance, or PM ATSR. The article says the office sits under the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Command and Control and Counter C2 and will develop, acquire, field, and sustain aerial and terrestrial sensors. Chris Manning, portfolio management executive for Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare, said the merger is meant to deliver integrated capabilities faster. Project Manager Tom Dunaway said the office will support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, target acquisition, and sensor integration for operations at installations and on the battlefield.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Army lab flew a hybrid-electric drone with a 3D-printed heavy-fuel engine
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 4 that researchers at the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Army Research Laboratory flew the VICTOR hybrid-electric drone with a heavy-fuel rotary engine developed using metal 3D printing. Tom's Hardware said the engine drives a 400-volt motor-generator that electrically drives the propellers, and that the drone uses JP-8. It quoted Dr. Kweon, an Army Research Laboratory researcher, telling Army.mil that 3D metal printing let the team redesign components from experimentation, build an air-cooled engine, and drop a bulky liquid-cooling system. Tom's Hardware said that iteration improved fuel atomization and decreased compression leaks.

items.headline: CECOM's Aberdeen year-in-review cites AI-assisted maintenance and installation IT/OT monitoring
items.summary: DVIDS posted a Nov. 2 story by Ann Gonzalez, datelined Aberdeen Proving Ground, saying the U.S. Army Communications-Electronics Command spent the past year synchronizing lifecycle support, modernization, and point-of-need maintenance. The article says the Integrated Logistics Support Center's AI-Assisted Maintenance effort gives Soldiers information support for equipment from tactical radios to tanks, and that Super Intelligence and telemaintenance let Soldiers troubleshoot without relying only on technical manuals or on-site experts. It says USAISEC's Project IRMA aims to put installation information-technology and operational-technology data, including power and cooling, into a common operating picture. It also says Tobyhanna Army Depot started a brushless-motor line in summer 2026, and that two of those motors powered a small uncrewed aircraft for eight hours, 41 minutes, and 43 seconds in a July demonstration.

items.headline: L3Harris receives a $36 million Army order for Hawkeye 4 Lite SATCOM terminals
items.summary: L3Harris said Nov. 3 in Melbourne, Florida, that it received a $36 million order in support of the U.S. Army for the Hawkeye 4 Lite satellite communications terminal. The company said the order will field under the Command and Control Network Optimized for Warfighting initiative, which it calls C2NOW, to improve secure SATCOM interoperability between the United States and NATO partners. Faisal Munir, president of Mission Critical Communications, said L3Harris is ready to support the Army with resilient, expeditionary communications that align with its modernization priorities. L3Harris said the Army configuration uses a rapidly deployable Hawkeye 4 Lite terminal with field-swappable components.

items.headline: USAISEC, with NETCOM, is replacing Army wide-area network gear in the U.S. and Europe
items.summary: An Army.mil article datelined Aberdeen Proving Ground on Oct. 26 says the U.S. Army Information Systems Engineering Command, a Communications-Electronics Command subordinate, is leading lifecycle replacement of wide-area network equipment across the United States and Europe in coordination with Network Enterprise Technology Command. The article says the work is meant to produce one software-defined enterprise network, using software-defined wide-area network technology and next-generation firewalls so the network can shift around outages, congestion and cyber threats without manual intervention. It says the design is a zero-trust model and that USAISEC engineers check power, cooling and shielding before new hardware goes in. Director of the Data Science and Engineering Directorate Dr. Jennifer Mills said the switches, servers and firewalls are the bedrock of the Army's digital future. USAISEC is headquartered at Fort Huachuca and uses hubs at Fort Huachuca and Fort Gordon.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: NATO tested commercial 5G towers as passive drone sensors in Latvia
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 2 that NATO's Digital Backbone Experimentation exercise, DiBaX 2026, ran in Latvia from Oct. 19 to Oct. 30 and investigated whether commercial 5G towers could passively detect and track drones. Admiral Pierre Vandier, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, said the exercise connected systems that were never designed to communicate, including a Maven system speaking to a national system, and that agentic AI fixed that link in hours. Tom's Hardware says the United States was among the allies in the exercise, and that some of the Latvia tests failed. It also says AT&T and Ericsson separately demonstrated 5G drone detection near AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, with drones flying between 300 and 400 feet.

items.headline: Army selects AWS and WWT for a $2.6 million Project Griffin cyber pilot
items.summary: Army Public Affairs said Oct. 26 that the Army selected Amazon Web Services and World Wide Technology on Oct. 23 for a Project Griffin pilot valued at a combined $2.6 million. The release says the aim is an autonomous, agentic platform so cyber defenders can neutralize threats faster, and that Griffin is one of three accelerated efforts under Project ARDS, the Army Rapid Defensive of Cyber Systems initiative. Principal cyber advisor Brandon Pugh said the Army will implement what he called SI-enabled tools to detect, divert and deceive threat actors. Project Manager, Cyber Warfare, under the Portfolio Management Executive for Intelligence and Spectrum Warfare, will manage execution, with contract support from Army Contracting Command-Aberdeen Proving Ground.

items.headline: Army Contracting Command-Rock Island awards Avum $61 million for contracting software
items.summary: The Department of War's Nov. 4 contracts release says Avum of Agoura Hills, California, was awarded a $61,053,453 firm-fixed-price contract for software sustainment, capability delivery, technical refactoring of the Virtual Contracting Enterprise business intelligence suite into a modern microservices architecture, and deployment of a secure contracting capability. The release says six bids were received, work will be performed in Agoura Hills, and the estimated completion date is Nov. 3, 2031. It says $2,818,452 in fiscal 2027 Army operation and maintenance funds were obligated at award. Army Contracting Command, Rock Island Arsenal, Illinois, is the contracting activity on W519TC-27-C-A019.

items.headline: Serco says it won an Army task order to field modernized command posts
items.summary: Serco said Nov. 3 that it was awarded a task order under the Army's Responsive Strategic Sourcing for Services contract to support Command Post Modernization. The release does not state a dollar value. Serco said the work expands a role it has held since 2019 and covers program management, engineering, integration, testing, logistics, training, and sustainment, including integrating hardware and software onto tactical vehicles and installing A-kit components. Amanda Miller, vice president for Serco North America's Systems Integration and Installation portfolio, said the work is meant to increase deployment speed, survivability, and technical innovation. Serco said it expects to add more than 200 positions.

items.headline: Army Contracting Command-Rock Island awards Pegasystems a $419 million enterprise software IDIQ
items.summary: ClearanceJobs on Oct. 30 printed an Army contract entry: Pegasystems Inc. of Waltham, Massachusetts, was awarded a $419,008,836 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity enterprise contract for commercial software subscriptions, technical support, and outcome-based professional services. The entry says one bid was solicited and one was received, that work locations and funding will be set with each order, that the estimated completion date is Oct. 28, 2036, and that Army Contracting Command, Rock Island, Illinois, is the contracting activity on W519TC-27-D-A019. GovConWire reported Nov. 2 that the Department of War announced the award Thursday, and that orders can cover the Pega Government Platform, direct Tier-3 support, and professional services for Capability Program Executive Enterprise Software and Services at Fort Belvoir, including case management, low-code application building, and acquisition modernization.
